approach.method_basis: The Parent runs two local molecular searches. Each region builds bounded graph-edit paths from a scored center and its own accepted descendants, fits a count-fingerprint Gaussian process to its episode records, and competes for evaluations through correlated Thompson samples in raw score units. A response amplitude computed from the entire current-session accepted archive is shared by both regions. Purchased progress controls each region’s radius and eventual restart. At a natural restart, the Parent chooses another already-scored root, resets ownership and progress state, and fits the restarted model to that root alone.
approach.novelty: Add fixed nearby accepted context to the predictor at each natural restart: the selected root and its nine nearest previously accepted neighbors condition the local model alongside subsequently owned records. Borrowed observations never become donors, owned feedback or controller successes. This addresses loss of predictive information at a new episode after shared amplitude already restored reset feedback. No evaluated same-Parent siblings are listed in the frozen brief. The concurrent restart-center proposal changes where an episode begins; this proposal keeps that root rule and changes what its predictor knows.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior in code Parent n-7d1e6230ecce is information loss at restart, not blanket restart starvation. All 19 actual restarts received immediate feedback, but all first-reset fields had one training label and constant mean equal to the root score. The frozen root-plus-nine-neighbor selected-stream audit covers 186 actually bought first-reset labels: RMSE falls from 0.3175198469903094 to 0.25338367925576977, MAE from 0.22077670112539952 to 0.15790520520149648, and SSE falls in each of the 19 episodes. The underlying Parent log and trajectory hashes, context availability, singleton means and accepted-label joins were verified across all fifteen frozen cells in policy/scratch/r0052-01-improve-L01/evidence-manifest.json and its per-cell audit files; zero-reset cells are retained. This retrospective prediction comparison identifies an actionable conditioning loss, not calibrated uncertainty, unbought utility or an alternative adaptive trajectory. Parent Analyze records post-reset GLOBAL gain 0.11690985499057077/950 = 0.0001230630052532324 and late-half mass 0.8322070529143051/2175, despite its whole-panel gain over n-bc1f80092068. Its macro mean 0.58461375649735 (population SD 0.01681763193120207; seed macros 0.593252148691163, 0.599485254783125, 0.561103866017762) remains 0.022416559713781 below formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de. The earlier full-controller conversion refutation in n-bc1f80092068 remains intact.

adoptions.applicability: The Parent has accepted labels near its restart root but trains a singleton predictor. Local conditioning is therefore applicable to this specific information-loss bottleneck. The fixed neighbor subset is an adaptation supported by the frozen selected-stream audit, not a claim that it optimizes prediction or improves future utility.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Condition a local predictor on nearby available observations rather than discard known context at a new local episode.

deviations.adopted_setting: Fixed root-centered count-fingerprint subset, root plus nine already accepted neighbors, held for the restarted molecular episode; no ALC/MSPE optimization, integrated likelihood or hyperparameter fit.
deviations.paper_setting: Local Gaussian-process subsets for computer-experiment prediction, including sequential design criteria that can outperform simple geometric nearest neighbors.
deviations.reason: The frozen ticket tests whether existing nearby information improves this singleton reset, while preserving its model and controller. It does not reproduce the paper’s design strategy or guarantee an optimal subset.

deviations.adopted_setting: Predictor membership is explicitly separated from molecular donor/controller ownership; new labels are only actual budgeted feedback and initial-episode fits remain unchanged.
deviations.paper_setting: Subset membership supports prediction in an emulation problem.
deviations.reason: The scientific intervention is predictive conditioning across an episode boundary, so borrowed labels must not create synthetic feedback, support or progress.

adoptions.implementation_change: Evolution.restart_retired freezes the unchanged root plus nine nearest distinct accepted records using count-Morgan generalized Tanimoto and earliest-serial ties; fit_region passes their canonical union with current owned records to the unchanged FingerprintPosterior.fit. Context remains fixed through the episode and enters neither donors nor control credit.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse only the frozen Search Policy review’s local-conditioning source, recorded query and method entry. The paper’s abstract and primary full text were reopened; they motivate local data selection while warning that nearest neighbors need not be optimal. The Parent’s measured singleton reset and actual selected-label replay motivate this fixed ten-record adaptation. Its GP conditioning, decision effect and real gain conversion remain separate prospective claims. No new assets, dependencies, learned hyperparameters, purchased initialization or additional intervention is introduced.

sources.applicability: Adopt only local accepted-data conditioning. Our fixed root-centered ten-record context uses molecular count similarity and persists through an episode; it does not implement ALC/MSPE design, integrated likelihood or learned hyperparameters. Selected-stream replay supports this adaptation, not source-paper performance transfer.
sources.finding: Nearest-neighbor local conditioning is a pragmatic baseline; the paper develops more elaborate sequential design criteria because geometric neighbors alone need not be optimal.
sources.title: Local Gaussian process approximation for large computer experiments (Gramacy and Apley)

hypothesis: Restart-local accepted-context conditioning. Only when the existing controller naturally restarts a region, retain the unchanged selected root plus the nine nearest distinct records already accepted in this Objective Session, ordered by descending inherited count-Morgan generalized Tanimoto to that root and then ascending accepted serial. Freeze this auxiliary context for the whole episode. Fit the unchanged local GP on the canonical-identity union of that context and the current episode-owned records. The context provides local score variation and changes conditional means/covariance before the raw-unit Thompson auction; the shared accepted-archive amplitude law is unchanged. Borrowed membership conveys no ownership, donor access, new feedback, center update or progress-counter credit.

finding_summary.headline: Restart context changed decisions and reduced prediction error; the interrupted panel leaves reliable benefit open.
finding_summary.insights: Nearby accepted observations really can restore predictive variation at a restart without giving borrowed labels control over the search. This settles the registered information-loss intervention at the execution and direct-behavior layers; it does not settle reliable three-seed benefit or rehabilitate the earlier full-controller conversion hypothesis. The literature-derived local-conditioning element operated, but this fixed molecular nearest-neighbor subset did not implement the source paper’s sequential design criteria or establish that geometric neighbors are the best subset. Better prediction error is only a partial explanation of search usefulness. On the 48 batches where both rank correlations were defined, average selected-label correlation was 0.409289 with context versus 0.406474 without it; 20 batches improved, 25 worsened and three tied. Only eight of 597 post-reset evaluations increased the global best, and one first-reset sitagliptin purchase supplied 62.1% of all post-reset gain. That molecule was also selected by the owned-only replay at the same Child state. The changed choices therefore establish a decision effect, while the passive replay cannot assign unbought outcomes or establish which earlier changes produced the later score advantage. The complete-panel causal contribution remains open. The molecular evidence also limits the method diagnosis. Formal scaffold variety coexists with repeated local chemical families: the median task generated 393 typed scaffolds in the two complete seeds, yet its strongest values remained in closely related nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl/amine structures. Conventional amine chemistry is reachable, but the other high-scoring series frequently retain N-halogen bonds, and both very small fragments and oversized recombinations remain. Restart memory alone does not supply coherent alternative functional-group arrangements. A context-selection or surrogate method that improves ranking would address the predictive limitation; a proposal operator that makes coherent scaffold and linker substitutions would address the chemical limitation. The present evidence identifies those distinct capabilities, not a demonstrated score benefit from either. The unchanged no-reset streams also bound applicability: this mechanism cannot affect a session before a natural restart.
finding_summary.results: The conditioning and decision mechanism is confirmed on the observed executions. All 13 natural restarts used the root plus nine previously accepted neighbors; first-fit training rose from one owned label to ten predictor labels, and all 13 first fields became nonconstant. The context stayed fixed, with no detected ownership, donor or controller contamination. Across 64 post-reset fields, exact posterior and sample reconstruction passed the registered tolerance; 54 of 60 exposed auctions changed the purchased set. On 129 actual first-reset labels, RMSE fell from 0.317030 with the owned-only replay to 0.294915 with context, and MAE fell from 0.211978 to 0.189050. Across all 597 post-reset labels, RMSE fell from 0.257217 to 0.254237. For complete seeds 0 and 2, post-reset global gain was 0.099398 over 597 evaluations, or 0.000166496 per evaluation, versus the matched Parent’s 0.054802 over 599, or 0.000091490. The available macro mean was 0.581637577 with population SD 0.011614516; its matched improvement was 0.004459570, comprising essentially no change in seed 0 and +0.008919195 in seed 2. Four task/seed endpoints improved, one declined and five tied. Seed-2 sitagliptin supplied 88.9% of positive endpoint gains. Both complete seed macros remained below the formal Anchor, with a matched mean deficit of 0.036290989. Seed 1 ended with Slurm time-limit cancellation, exit 143, after only ten recorded optimizer evaluations in zaleplon and before any observed restart. Its remaining tasks and all five final endpoints are unavailable. This technical interruption does not refute the executed mechanism, but the complete-panel +0.002 test, full-panel useful-context falsifier and formal task-safety result remain unevaluable.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich local series retain ordinary amine chemistry alongside N-halogen liabilities, tiny fragments and oversized products; coverage is partial.
molecular.overall_character: This assessment concerns the observed output of n-f3e58c614c9d, compared with code Parent n-7d1e6230ecce. Child seeds 0 and 2 each supply all five 300-row trajectories. Seed 1 supplies only 20 zaleplon_mpo rows, including ten initial records and ten optimizer proposals; its summary is absent and execution receipt records exit 143/status retryable. Its other four task trajectories are absent. Thus context.comparison.child_complete=false and paired_complete=false remain controlling: the available complete comparisons are seeds 0 and 2, not a completed three-seed panel. All fifteen published Parent Search trajectories were available and read, including seed 1; Parent seed-1 endpoints cannot be paired with completed Child endpoints. No held-out or Confirmation evidence was used. Across available Child trajectories there are 3020 recorded molecules including 2910 optimizer proposals. The digest shows ring-closure rates 0.9379-0.9897 and aromatic-text rates 0.9155-0.9845 across tasks, with zero explicit charge and stereocentre rates. These are molecule-level SMILES indicators, not perceived ring or aromatic-atom fractions. The output contains substantial aromatic/fused-ring chemistry, carbonyl and ether groups, cyclic and acyclic amines, and many halogen substitutions. Ordinary medicinal scaffolds coexist with N-halogen bonds, strained or enlarged rings, very small fragments, and oversized recombinations. Parseability does not establish stability or a practical synthesis. Structural diversity is moderate as a chemical judgement: many formal scaffolds exist, but the leading molecules cluster within particular seed-specific series, and ring distortions contribute to formal novelty. All descriptor counts below were calculated in memory from the directly read authorized trajectories using RDKit, only on optimizer rows in complete seeds 0 and 2 unless explicitly stated. Size is heavy-atom count; tails mean <6 and >50 heavy atoms. Typed/generic coverage means distinct canonical Murcko scaffold SMILES and their all-carbon generic counterparts, counting the empty acyclic scaffold once. Parent counts use the same two seeds. Reported endpoint similarities use unhashed radius-two Morgan count vectors and dot/(squared-norm sum minus dot); endpoint pairs all have at least six heavy atoms, so fragments are excluded. These are structural diagnostics, not rewards or component attribution. Child provenance is the exact frozen request policy/requests/r0052-01-improve-L01-molecular-assess-486caa0d28a2fe78.json, its context.molecular_digest and trusted context.citation_trajectory_paths; source/evaluation/seed identify quoted records. Parent comparisons use the individual published trajectory files named in each task entry. No new audit artifact was written and no existing audit was altered.

per_task.generated_character: The completed streams center on moderately sized, fused N-heteroaromatic systems with aryl substituents. Seed 2 reaches an ethoxy/methyl/thiol-substituted indole carboxamide bearing an N-bromo-N-phenyl amide: its best molecule has 24 heavy atoms and three perceived aromatic rings. The corresponding N-fluoro and N-chloro variants also appear among the leaders. Seed 0 instead ends with a compact fused nitrogen-rich aryl system bearing an N-chloro aryl-enamine connection. The partial seed-1 leader is a more conventional cyano/dimethoxy indole arylcarboxamide with a fluoromethyl substituent and no N-halogen bond. Complete-seed heavy atoms span 2-58, median 25; the small/large tails contain 23/1 of 580 proposals. Typed/generic scaffolds are 186/112 versus Parent 175/107; 393 of 580 proposals contain a direct N-halogen bond. Digest ring/aromatic rates are 0.9593/0.9508, including the partial seed-1 stream. The completed output is ring-rich but often chemically questionable because of its N-halogen substitution.
liabilities: Frequent N-halogen amide/enamine bonds and a free aryl thiol raise chemical-stability and synthesis questions; the score does not measure those properties.
Low-scoring tiny fragments and ring-opening products coexist with the useful aromatic series; nominal scaffold novelty is not uniformly coherent molecular design.
missing_features: Completed leading series do not demonstrate a comparably explored set of conventional, non-N-halogen replacements preserving the favorable intact heteroaromatic/carboxamide arrangement; the partial nitrile carboxamide shows that such chemistry is available.

The observed gradient favors particular intact substitution patterns, but these trajectories do not identify a specific absent target core or prove that adding another functional group would improve the score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-2 N-Br/N-F/N-Cl carboxamides all score 0.44813028323800735: the observed scores do not distinguish those halogens. An otherwise close fluoromethoxy analogue, Cc1c(S)c(OCF)cc2[nH]c(C(=O)N(Br)c3ccccc3)cc12, scores 0.20918448806108078, showing a local preference associated with the ethoxy-bearing arrangement rather than halogen presence alone. Ringless ClCl and small C1CSO1 score 0; final partly opened indole-ring variants score 0.3406238448634823 and 0.29455732743255275. The partial seed-1 conventional nitrile carboxamide scores 0.4407194967701815, so N-halogen bonding is not necessary for a relatively high value in the observed data. Against Parent, completed seed-0 Top1 is 0.42570769607214154 versus 0.42762099872850584, and seed-2 Top1 is 0.44813028323800735 versus 0.4478476056206344; both remain in related aromatic N-halogen chemistry. Endpoint count similarities are 0.806283/0.707921 for seeds 0/2. Seed 1 supports only partial chemistry, not an endpoint comparison.

per_task.generated_character: Both completed streams are heteroaromatic and carbonyl-rich, with more molecular growth than the other tasks. The seed-2 leader has 40 heavy atoms and four perceived aromatic rings: two fused nitrogen/oxygen-containing bicyclic units joined through NH, with ketone side chains, chloromethyl functionality and an unsaturated imine-bearing side chain. Seed 0 favors a 32-heavy-atom, four-ring heteroaromatic assembly containing a bicyclic dione, aza rings and several halogens. Complete-seed heavy atoms span 2-108, median 43; small/large tails are 11/197 of 580 proposals. Typed/generic scaffolds are 305/242, exactly the Parent counts. Digest ring and aromatic rates are both 0.9776. Many graphs are formally diverse, but the very large tail and multifunctional linkages make general synthetic plausibility questionable.
liabilities: Large repeated heteroaromatic/carbonyl assemblies and chloromethyl/imine side chains add synthesis and stability concerns; actual synthesis and stability were not tested.
Both the oversized tail and small carbonyl-halide/halocarbon proposals are present; a common 0.5 score for tiny molecules does not make them suitable medicinal structures.
missing_features: The leading examples do not supply a comparably scoring compact series that retains the linked heteroaromatic acceptor arrangement with fewer potentially labile side chains.

Several peripheral changes tie the observed maximum. The evidence does not reveal a particular absent motif that would lift this local plateau, and does not justify adding rings or mass indiscriminately.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The linked heteroaromatic carbonyl assembly reaches 0.6314459049544995. Changing chloromethyl to bromomethyl or adding chlorine beside a ketone can leave that value unchanged. Replacing one ketone-side-chain carbon connection with an amide-like nitrogen connection gives 0.6027917030768524, while changing the imine side chain to an amine-containing chain gives 0.61634565330557. These are local associations favoring the retained core/linkage pattern; they do not establish a general reward for molecular bulk. Small C=C, FCCl and O=C(Cl)Cl all score 0.5. Both complete Child optimizer sequences are identical to their published Parent sequences, including endpoints 0.6105466720544941/0.6314459049544995 and endpoint similarities 1/1. No Child seed-1 trajectory exists. per_task.generated_character: The highest observed seed-2 molecule is a compact 19-heavy-atom N-propyl azetidine connected through methylene to an amino/phenol-substituted indane: three rings, including one aromatic ring. Nearby leaders contain a pyrrolidine and longer chlorinated linkers. Seed 0 instead favors an acyclic tertiary amino group attached to a substituted cyclohexene bearing a dichlorophenyl group; its leader has 24 heavy atoms and two rings. These are substantially more recognizable amine/aromatic medicinal motifs than many other task leaders. Complete-seed heavy atoms span 1-108, median 27; small/large tails are 17/10 of 580. Typed/generic scaffolds are 247/157 versus Parent 246/155. Digest ring/aromatic rates are 0.969/0.9155. Conventional amine chemistry is demonstrably present, although some peripheral proposals remain unusual.
liabilities: Several saturated ring and linker stereocentres remain unspecified, limiting interpretation of any individual three-dimensional structure.
Some nearby candidates carry N-halogen or chlorinated aminal-like connections, while long alkyl/aryl combinations can be highly hydrophobic; these properties were not experimentally characterized.
missing_features: There is no observed general deficit of cyclic basic-amine candidates: the best molecule already contains one. The missing coverage is explicitly specified stereochemical variants of these substituted saturated rings.
No charged SMILES occur in the digest. Distinct protonation representations and their consequences are unmeasured; their absence does not establish that the objective would reward them.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact phenol/aniline/azetidine molecule scores 0.9999975203517744; a related chlorinated pyrrolidine/linker analogue scores 0.996569840364855. In contrast, the dichlorophenyl vinyl sulfone scores 0.0002798384720262442 and small N-fluoro azetidine CCC1C(C)CN1F scores 0.0026894518256264568. The observed high-scoring molecules combine an accessible non-amide amine with substantial cyclic/aromatic structure; the low examples show that neither an aromatic ring nor a small nitrogen ring alone suffices. This is structural association, not an inferred binding pose or activity claim. Seed-0 Child and Parent optimizer sequences are identical, ending at 0.9794504645558658. Seed 2 changes from Parent Top1 0.9970518791461749 to the compact Child leader, with endpoint count similarity 0.728972; seed-0 similarity is 1. Seed 1 is absent for Child. per_task.generated_character: These streams contain the richest formal scaffold variation, but leaders remain complex nitrogen-rich polycycles. The seed-2 leader has 34 heavy atoms and five perceived rings, combining an ethoxy aza-aromatic/four-membered adjacent-dicarbonyl unit with a phenyl-substituted fused nitrogen heterocycle and an eight-membered amine ring. Seed 0 ends at a 30-heavy-atom, four-ring assembly with a fused aromatic core and an eleven-membered carbonyl/oxygen/hydrazine-containing ring. Complete-seed heavy atoms span 1-59, median 31; small/large tails are 6/7 of 580. Typed/generic scaffolds are 393/268 versus Parent 386/269. Digest ring/aromatic rates are 0.9897/0.9845. Extensive ring content is clear, but strained dicarbonyl and enlarged N-N-containing rings make routine synthetic plausibility uncertain.
liabilities: Adjacent carbonyls on a four-membered ring raise strain/reactivity questions; their presence alone is not proof of impossibility.
Large heterocyclic closures and N-N bonds in another leading family complicate synthesis and conformational interpretation; no synthesis routes or conformer-specific validation are supplied.
missing_features: The leading examples do not demonstrate a simpler, chemically conventional scaffold preserving the apparently favorable relative placement of aromatic, amine and carbonyl environments.

Many formal scaffold changes give only nearby values. The missing capability is controlled replacement of the complete functional-group arrangement, not basic access to ring closures; the trajectories do not identify a specific unmade rewarded scaffold.

A closely related shorter amine-ring analogue scores 0.22653712064247994; expanding the linker between ring systems gives 0.2219851851177253. Thus local topology/linker changes have small effects within this series. More rings alone is not an established direction. Child seed-2 best is the same as Parent; seed 0 changes from Parent 0.21592303267069837 to 0.2178360563647521 with related enlarged-ring chemistry. per_task.generated_character: The strongest seed-0 family is a fluorinated nitrogen-rich bicyclic dione bearing unsaturated five-membered rings and an aminomethyl substituent. Its leader has 29 heavy atoms, four perceived rings and three direct N-F bonds. The completed seed-2 leader instead has 28 heavy atoms, an aza-aromatic partner, a thiocarbonyl/carbonyl-containing N-fluoro ring, and several exocyclic unsaturated fluorinated chains. Complete-seed heavy atoms span 1-59, median 28; small/large tails are 24/4 of 580 proposals. Typed/generic scaffolds are 142/71 versus Parent 151/79; 441 of 580 proposals contain a direct N-halogen bond. Digest ring/aromatic rates are 0.9379/0.9345. These products have drug-sized skeletons but unusually heavy reliance on chemically questionable N-halogen arrangements.
liabilities: Multiple N-F bonds, N-S alternatives and highly unsaturated thiocarbonyl arrangements raise stability and synthesis concerns that high benchmark scores do not resolve.
Some large recombinations and atom-sized fragments consume observed proposals despite extremely small scores; adding fluorine or increasing size is not a sufficient molecular design rule.
missing_features: The leading fluorinated families do not demonstrate comparably scoring conventional replacements for their multiple N-F bonds while retaining the local size, polarity and carbon-bound fluorination pattern.

The generator does not specify stereochemistry in the substituted partially saturated rings. No reward for stereochemical resolution or for any absent target-specific motif is established by these trajectories.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-0 fluorinated dione scores 0.7327195754462501; replacing one terminal carbon-bound F with sulfur gives 0.7098514946189204. Seed 2 reaches 0.5439029627880493 in the unsaturated thiocarbonyl series, while a close chain-extended analogue scores 0.3100765517131085. The data favor a constrained arrangement/size and fluorinated composition within these local families, without establishing the score components or a necessary N-F bond. The 59-heavy-atom ester/aryl/carboxamide recombination scores 2.3956869936426998e-105, while single-atom F scores 1.1043196211273875e-26: both size extremes can be very poor. Seed 2 moves from Parent 0.5025353058534101 in a related fluorinated bicyclic dione family to the Child thiocarbonyl leader; endpoint similarities are 1/0.594286 for seeds 0/2. transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-f3e58c614c9d, observed Search output only: the completed arylcarboxamide stream contains 393 direct N-halogen molecules among 580 proposals, and the fluorinated dione stream contains 441 among 580. Leading examples contain N-Br/N-Cl amides or multiple N-F bonds. A partial-stream nitrile arylcarboxamide without an N-halogen bond scores 0.4407194967701815, so conventional alternatives are possible. This is a chemical association under incomplete three-seed coverage, not attribution to the conditioning component.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve conventional heteroatom functional groups while varying otherwise useful ring systems.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Develop chemically coherent substitutions and ring/linker changes that retain ordinary amide, amine and carbon-bound halogen environments. Compare such alternatives through the current session actual labels; do not treat N-halogen removal as an established score improvement or encode any objective identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-f3e58c614c9d, complete Search seeds 0 and 2: the linked heteroaromatic stream has 11 proposals below six heavy atoms and 197 above fifty among 580; the fluorinated dione stream has 24 and 4 respectively. Other streams also retain both tails. Observed low molecules include ClCl, methane and single-atom F, while an oversized aryl/ester recombination has score 2.3956869936426998e-105. Larger heteroaromatic molecules can still be useful, so these observations do not define a universal optimum size.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve useful molecular scale when recombining or fragmenting structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support de novo edits that change one coherent functional substructure without uncontrolled whole-scaffold deletion or multiplication. Use accepted local feedback to distinguish useful growth from destructive fragmentation; any universal size restriction would require its own evidence.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-f3e58c614c9d, complete Search seeds 0 and 2: one N-rich polycyclic stream contains 393 typed and 268 generic Murcko scaffolds, yet its leading observed values remain 0.2266386345140889 and 0.22653712064247994 in closely related dicarbonyl/amine frameworks. Other leading families recur with N-halogen swaps, ring expansions or unsaturated linkers. The Parent comparison retains many of the same families; this is not evidence that the generator cannot form rings or that the current component caused the limitation.
transferable_gaps.gap: Formal ring diversity exceeds demonstrated access to coherent alternative functional-group arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand chemically coherent scaffold and linker substitutions that preserve useful observed functional-group relationships while changing their topology. method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
